rationale: This study uses COMSOL Multiphysics numerical modeling to simulate physical and microbial riverbed clogging, hydraulic disconnection between rivers and aquifers, and biogeochemical migration of iron and manganese in sediment pore water. Note that 'disconnections' here refers to hydrological river-aquifer disconnection rather than household utility disconnection. It involves pure hydraulic/biogeochemical engineering modeling with no household/community water or sanitation service access, no legal or administrative mechanism, and no service-access outcome (E06).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings: the study is a pure hydraulic and biogeochemical numerical simulation (COMSOL Multiphysics) of river-aquifer hydraulic disconnection and Fe/Mn reactive transport, with no legal, administrative, institutional, or governance dimension.

evidence_quotes.quote: Evolution of river-aquifer disconnections and the migration and transformation of iron and manganese
This study developed a model using the COMSOL Multiphysics platform to characterize the riverbed clogging-groundwater exploitation-disconnection process
